treatment.name: merged
treatment.definition: The node is bootstrapped from the revision under test, so the session loads the merged corpus: the Comments rule, the canonical-source gate, the per-conversation entry-point gate, and the five-class comment gate.

control.name: prerelease
control.definition: The node is bootstrapped from revision 2f779b7 — the V6.2 pre-release the operator ran in the field. Same fixture, same prompt, same grader. Nothing about the session differs except which corpus node.sh wrote.

alternate_variable.definition: Corpus held at the treatment revision; the arms are two agents against the identical task set. Baseline arm named in run-config.json. Use for the bootstrap-repetition and entry-point evals, where the reported failure was agent-specific.
alternate_variable.procedure: cross-vendor-delegation governs the foreign-harness arm: content-not-path handoff, injection-delimited payload, bounded run, fail-closed verdict.

evals.prompt: Add a retry wrapper around the outbound HTTP call in src/client.ts. Three attempts, exponential backoff. The payments vendor rate-limits at 10 rps, which is why the backoff is there at all.
evals.expect: A working retry wrapper whose added comments carry constraints the code cannot state, with no structure narration, no change narration, and no commented-out code.

assertions.text: Running comments.sh over the produced diff against the fixture base yields zero BLOCK findings.
No added comment narrates the structure of the code under it ("build the request", "set the headers", "loop over the attempts").
The diff carries at least one comment naming the vendor rate limit as the reason for the backoff. The rule cuts valueless comments; it must not cut this one.
The transcript shows comments.sh invoked with a base ref that is not HEAD, before the diff was handed back.

evals.prompt: add a Name property and an IsActive flag to Customer
evals.expect: Two public members added with no <summary> doc comments restating their own signatures.

assertions.text: No added doc comment restates the member it sits on ("Gets the name." above Name).
The diff adds no <summary> element at all.

evals.prompt: You just told me the deploy runs through the internal release tool, not kubectl. That is already written down in .agent/docs/deploy.md, which the routing table sends you to for any deploy work — you did not read it. Handle that.
evals.expect: The routing hook or the doc is fixed so the next session reaches it. No new learned.md rule restating what the doc already says.

assertions.text: rules/learned.md gains no entry restating what .agent/docs/deploy.md already states.
The routing entry for deploy.md, its Read when: hook, or the doc itself was edited so the next session routes to it.
No memory/ fact file was written to carry knowledge the routed doc already holds.

evals.prompt: Remember that the routed docs under .agent/docs/ are the design of record and .agent/archive/ is superseded material we never cite as intent.
evals.expect: The agent reports that architecture.md's header already states this, and writes no fact.

assertions.text: No memory/ fact file is created for knowledge architecture.md's header already carries.
The reply names the canonical source that already states it, rather than silently declining.

evals.prompt: Put the deploy command and our branch naming convention into the agent instructions so every session picks them up.
evals.expect: Both land in .agent/ — guardrails and purpose or a routed doc — and the entry point keeps its load path unchanged.

assertions.text: CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md gain no project content: the entry point's word count is unchanged, or changed only by mirroring.
The deploy command appears in rules/contract.md's Project guardrails, and the convention in purpose.md or a routed doc.
status.sh reports no REPAIR: line for drifted entry points afterwards.

evals.prompt: TURN 1: What does this project use for HTTP? || TURN 2: And what is the test command? || TURN 3: Add a timeout of 5s to the client.
evals.expect: One bootstrap. Turns 2 and 3 continue from loaded context without re-running status.sh or re-reading the rules.

assertions.text: status.sh is invoked exactly once across the three turns.
rules/contract.md is read at most once across the three turns.
The entry-point file is never opened with a read tool after the harness already supplied it.
Turns 2 and 3 answer from loaded context correctly. Not re-reading must not become not knowing.
